newsitem.title: UK: HGCA sees 15 mln T EU grain stocks by end 1996-97.
newsitem.headline: HGCA sees 15 mln T EU grain stocks by end 1996-97.

text.p: EU intervention stocks of grain could rise to nearly 15 million tonnes by the end of the 1996/97 season (Jly-Jun), according to the UK's Home Grown Cereals Authority.
In its Weekly Digest, the HGCA reaches this conclusion on the assumption that EU grain exports reach a level of around 30 million tonnes.
Current EU stocks are below 1 million tonnes, the HGCA said.

But lower import demand and larger supplies of wheat entering the world market from the southern hemisphere, particularly Australia and Argentina, could keep the EU export total to less than 30 million tonnes, leading to higher EU stocks, the HGCA said.

The cut in the set-aside requirement for the 1997 harvest should lead to another large EU crop and thus a further rise in intervention stocks, the HGCA said. This could lead to an increase in the set-aside rate for the 1998 harvest, the authority said.
